frozenBefore: 1.1.1 amends 1.1.0 AFTER sight of the 1.1.0 results and after the independent V12 review (finding SPXPOP m4: Broadcom Corp. -> Broadcom Ltd. 2015-09 -> 2016-03 chained as one identity with +200 %). Correction after independent review; the 1.1.0 files are kept unchanged (population/periods/validation/summary/manifest-1.1.0) and stay loadable (ruleVersion option).

inputs.snapshots: INDEXPOP private snapshots.json (335 validated fund-date holdings schedules; rules-1.0.0 of INDEXPOP)
inputs.mapping: INDEXPOP private mapping-1.2.0.json (key -> securityId per date (T1/T2 only), CIK)
inputs.fates: INDEXPOP private fates-1.2.0.json (= repo exits-1.2.0.json.gz with names)
inputs.series: quant/data/market/discover-series-long/ref_*.json (weekly split-adjusted closes, provider split factors), read-only
inputs.fundTotalReturn: N-PORT returnInfo/monthlyTotReturns of the same holdings documents (2019+), used only as secondary reference

price: p = value / shares of the position in the holdings schedule (fund valuation at the holdings date). No external price is used for members present at both dates.

identityChain.scope: consecutive holdings dates t0 < t1 of the same fund
order: C1_CUSIP: same valid CUSIP (N-PORT) or, when the CUSIP is missing/zero, same valid ISIN

C2_NAME: same normalized name key + share class (INDEXPOP lib.cjs normName), unique among the still unmatched positions on both sides; duplicate keys inside one schedule are paired by the smallest |log(p1/p0) - log(1+Ridx_prelim)|
C3_CIK: same CIK (INDEXPOP mapping) for the t0 key and the t1 key, unique among the still unmatched positions on both sides

C4_FUZZY: token-set Jaccard of normalized names >= 0.6, unique best candidate in both directions among the still unmatched, and price/share plausible: |log q| <= log(1.5) or q within the split tolerance of a split ratio, and |e_none| <= 0.7 or |e_split| <= 0.7
identityChain.breaks: An exit at t0 and an entry at t1 of the same fund that share a CIK or have token-set Jaccard >= 0.5 but were not linked by C1-C4 are counted as possible identity breaks (not linked, reported).
identityChain.identityBreak: 1.1.1: identity break at a merger. A link of tier C3_CIK or C4_FUZZY (no CUSIP/ISIN and no name-key identity) whose split class is SHARE_CHANGE or AMBIGUOUS_CA and for which, under every admissible return hypothesis R_h (the point return, or both bounds of AMBIGUOUS_CA), log(1 + R_h) - log(1 + Ridx_prelim) > log 2 holds, is NOT linked. Signature of a merger target chained to the acquirer's (new holding's) position via a shared CIK or a similar name. The t0 position is booked as BOUNDED_EXIT (point 0 %, lower bound -100 %, no upper bound) with fate IDENTITY_BREAK, without the exit cascade (no cross-fund, series or cash estimate); the t1 position becomes an entry. Downward discontinuities (spin-offs, special dividends, crashes) are not affected.

splitDetection.shareRatio: r = shares1 / shares0 for every linked position
splitDetection.fundFlow: F = median of r over C1/C2 links of the period
splitDetection.indexPrelim: Ridx_prelim = value-weighted (w0) mean of p1/p0 - 1 over C1/C2 links with |log q| < log(1.10)
splitDetection.ratioTolerance: |log q - log s| <= 0.15 for the nearest ratio s
splitDetection.residuals: e_split = log(s * p1/p0) - log(1 + Ridx_prelim); e_none = log(p1/p0) - log(1 + Ridx_prelim)

classes.SPLIT: trigger, nearest ratio within tolerance, |e_split| + 0.10 <= |e_none| and |e_split| <= 1.0: split factor s
classes.SHARE_CHANGE: trigger, (no ratio within tolerance, or |e_none| + 0.10 <= |e_split|) and |e_none| <= 1.0: split factor 1 (float/index-share change, issuance, merger)
classes.AMBIGUOUS_CA: otherwise: no point return, bounds = [min, max] of the return under s and under 1

splitDetection.validation: against the provider split factors of our weekly series (return-series.js#splitFactors convention: splits with t0 < split date <= t1) for links whose t0 and t1 keys map to the same securityId, and against cross-fund links of the same security and period (independent share counts)

periodReturn.definition: price return R = s * p1/p0 - 1 of every t0 member, weight w0 = value0 / sum(value0) over all members of the t0 schedule

statuses.OBS_CHAIN: linked in the own fund (C1-C4), split class NONE/SPLIT/SHARE_CHANGE
statuses.OBS_CROSSFUND: not linked in the own fund, but the same security (CUSIP/ISIN, name key or CIK at t0) is linked in another fund with exactly the same t0 and t1 (non-ambiguous there): that fund's return
statuses.OBS_SERIES: exit; mapped (T1/T2) at t0 to one of our series with a bar within 7 days on/before t0 and a bar within 7 days on/before t1: adjusted close ratio (weekly; documented misalignment)
statuses.EST_SERIES_END: exit; series ends between t0 and t1 and the INDEXPOP fate is ACQUIRED_OR_MERGED (or the lifecycle register has a terminal record): return to the last bar, cash at 0 % afterwards
statuses.EST_CASH: exit; lifecycle register CASH_MERGER for the mapped securityId or CIK with lastTradeDate in (t0, t1]: cashPerShare / p0 - 1
statuses.BOUNDED_EXIT: exit without any of the above: point value 0 % (last holdings price carried), lower bound -100 %, no upper bound; fate class from INDEXPOP (ACQUIRED_OR_MERGED, DELISTED_OTHER, DELISTED_BANKRUPTCY, STILL_REPORTING_INDEX_EXIT, NO_SEC_EVIDENCE, NO_CIK, TEMPORARY_ABSENCE, NOT_FATED; 1.1.1: IDENTITY_BREAK for unlinked identity breaks) is reported per case
statuses.BOUNDED_EXIT_SERIES_DELISTED: exit; series ends between t0 and t1 without acquisition evidence: point = return to last bar, lower bound -100 %, upper bound = point

periodReturn.indexLevel: Rpoint = sum w0 * point; Rlow = same with every bounded case at its lower bound; impliedBoundedMean = (Rfund - sum over observed/estimated w0*R) / bounded weight (diagnostic only)
periodReturn.statusOrder: for t0 members without an own-fund link: OBS_CROSSFUND, OBS_SERIES (series continues to t1), EST_CASH, EST_SERIES_END, BOUNDED_EXIT_SERIES_DELISTED, BOUNDED_EXIT
periodReturn.crossFundPriceCheck: OBS_CROSSFUND additionally requires |p0(own) / p0(other) - 1| <= 2 % at t0 (same security, same valuation date)
periodReturn.frozenTail: a series whose last >= 4 bars carry the identical close ends at the first bar of that run (carried-forward tail); a lifecycle register lastTradeDate for the securityId takes precedence
periodReturn.fateJoin: fate from INDEXPOP fates by fund + lastHoldingDate (= t0) + holdings name; a member absent at t1 but present at a later date of the same fund = TEMPORARY_ABSENCE; IWB/IWM exits have no SEC fate in INDEXPOP = NOT_FATED

consistency.externalReference: fund price return between the last trading day on/before t0 and t1 from the daily multi-asset series (SPY, QQQ, DIA, IWM); price return on both sides (dividends missing on both sides)
consistency.tolerance: 0.5 pp * sqrt(months / 3); months = calendar months between t0 and t1 (quarter 0.50, half year 0.71, 9 months 0.87, year 1.00)
consistency.approxReference_IWB_IWV: no IWB/IWV price series in the repository. N-PORT era (both dates N-PORT): Rfund_approx = compounded N-PORT monthly total return of the fund over the months of the period minus the SPY dividend gap of the same months (compounded SPY N-PORT total return - SPY price return); tolerance + 0.25 pp. Report era: no external reference; internal checks only (member-level agreement with the IWV chain for the same securities and dates; IWV vs IWB/IWM mix).
consistency.secondary: for every fund with N-PORT total returns at both dates: TR_nport - Rpoint (should be a small positive dividend yield); reported only
consistency.nportTotalReturn: only for periods of exactly 3 months whose t1 holdings document is N-PORT (monthly total returns of the 3 months ending at t1)

period.QUALIFIED: observed+estimated weight >= 97.0 %, bounded weight <= 3.0 %, and |error| <= tolerance (external or approximate reference)
period.QUALIFIED_INTERNAL: coverage criteria met, no external/approximate reference available, internal cross-fund agreement >= 99 % of the common weight with |dR| <= 0.1 pp
period.NOT_QUALIFIED_NO_REFERENCE: coverage criteria met, but neither an external/approximate reference nor the internal cross-fund agreement is available or met

qualification.population: A population qualifies on a span of consecutive periods when >= 90 % of its periods are QUALIFIED (or QUALIFIED_INTERNAL where no reference exists) and no two consecutive periods fail; the longest such span ending at the last period is reported together with every failing period. The span must start with a qualified period.

notApplicable.reason: price-weighted index: DIA holds the same share count of every member, a split does not change the fund's share count, so share-ratio split detection cannot work; periods are reported with qualification NOT_APPLICABLE_PRICE_WEIGHTED and no member data are published

limits: Frequency is the holdings frequency (annual/semiannual/quarterly); no weekly or monthly study is possible with this population alone.
Price return only; dividends are missing on both sides (fund price series are price returns as well).
Spin-offs are not modelled: the parent's price drop is a loss, the spun-off company enters at t1; this shows up as consistency error.
No fundamentals except via the CIK of the INDEXPOP mapping to the corrected PIT panel (research-pit-market-cap.cjs), where mapped.

changes: N-PORT total return only for 3-month periods
span starts with a qualified period
amendments.reason: implementation clarifications; none was prompted by an outcome

changes: ratios 25, 30, 40, 50 added (the registered set had the reverse ratios 1/25 ... 1/50 but not the forward ones)
findings: Real splits are linked with q off the ratio by more than 5 %: index share/float updates and the median fund-flow factor move q (Tesla 3:1 2022 q=3.18, Broadcom 10:1 2024 q=10.70, Nike/Omnicom/Yum 2:1 2006 q=1.81-1.90, BellSouth/Intel/Wal-Mart/IBM 2:1 1998-99 q=1.89-1.95). Under 1.0.1 these became SHARE_CHANGE (price halving booked as loss) or AMBIGUOUS_CA.

Ratios between 2/3 and 3/2 are produced by index reweighting, not splits: Nasdaq-100 capping (QQQ Tesla 0.8, Broadcom 2/3, Apple 3/4, Amazon 5/4), share issuance in 2008 (BB&T, Principal, Capital One 5/4). Under 1.0.1 the residual test accepted them as splits when the idiosyncratic return happened to match.
Booking Holdings 25:1 (2026, q = 24.47) fell outside the registered forward ratios and became AMBIGUOUS_CA (found in a first, unpublished 1.1.0 run with the other two changes).
DIA (price-weighted) cannot show a split in its share count (3M 2:1 2003, Visa 4:1 2015, Apple 4:1 2020 all q = 1).
amendments.reason: The tolerance and ratio set were chosen a priori without data; the 1.0.1 validation shows they mis-specify how index funds' share counts move. The change is limited to these two parameters and the DIA scope; margin, residual bound, statuses, references, tolerances and qualification criteria are unchanged. The provider-factor validation is therefore in-sample for 1.1.0; the cross-fund agreement and the fund consistency are the remaining checks, also seen.

amendments.prompt: independent V12 review, finding SPXPOP m4 (correction after independent review)
changes: identity break at mergers (identityChain.identityBreak): C3_CIK/C4_FUZZY link + SHARE_CHANGE/AMBIGUOUS_CA + price more than doubled relative to the index under every hypothesis -> not linked, t0 position BOUNDED_EXIT with fate IDENTITY_BREAK
fate IDENTITY_BREAK appended to the fate list
findings: Broadcom Corp. (Class A) was linked by CIK (C3) to Broadcom Ltd. in SPY 2015-09 -> 2016-03 (AMBIGUOUS_CA, both bounds +200 %), QQQ 2015-09 -> 2016-09 (+235 %), IWB/IWV 2015-12 -> 2016-06 (SHARE_CHANGE, +169 % as an observed return); the acquirer Avago became a BOUNDED_EXIT. Broadcom Corp. holders received cash plus Broadcom Ltd. shares; the chained price ratio is the price of a different security.

A scan of all links for the same signature finds 13 cases in all funds (Broadcom x4, PXRE -> Argo 2007 x2, BPZ Energy -> BPZ Resources 2007 x2, Arsanis -> X4 2019, WMIH -> Mr Cooper 2018, Aerovate -> Jade 2025, Cano Health 2023 and System1 2025 (reverse splits outside the ratio set)); all are treated the same way.
amendments.reason: A chained return of a different security is a false observation (the 1.1.0 identity chain had no plausibility bound for C3 links). The rule is limited to upward discontinuities on links without CUSIP/name identity; thresholds of the split rule, statuses, references and qualification criteria are unchanged.
